title: API surface specs and launch checklist for Chat/Completion/Embedding/Rerank
creator: Priya Patel
description: PRD and launch readiness checklist that defines the product requirements, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan for the hosted API surface covering Chat, Completions, Embeddings, and Rerank endpoints. This ticket consolidates API contracts, non-functional SLOs, SDK and docs deliverables, and a phased launch plan for GA. The objective is to deliver a developer-friendly, observable, and performant hosted API that supports streaming and synchronous flows where appropriate.
scope_changes: Initial scope reduced: Rerank will ship as synchronous only for GA; streaming/prefetch for rerank deferred to v2
Embeddings will support batched requests up to 512 items for GA; very-large-batch throughput improvements prioritized post-GA
Completions endpoint will support structured JSON outputs via shape hints in prompts; schema validation hooks are out-of-scope for GA
Streaming for Chat and Completions will be available for GA but with a documented best-effort latency SLO (stream start within 200ms for <64 token responses)
Default token quota and rate limits decided: free-tier = 500k tokens/month; paid tiers defined in pricing doc (link in artifacts)
acceptance_criteria: API contracts: /v1/chat, /v1/completions, /v1/embeddings, /v1/rerank documented with example requests/responses and SDK snippets
SDKs: JS and Python SDKs updated with end-to-end examples for all four endpoint types; integration tests pass in CI
Performance SLOs: median latency <= 120ms for completions (<= 256 tokens), streaming handshake < 200ms, embeddings batch latency <= 350ms for up to 16 items
Reliability: 99.95% availability for hosted API over a 30d window in staging and load tests; automatic fallback to compatible model variant on capacity constraints
Observability: dashboards for per-route latency, per-model cost breakdown, error rate, and token consumption; SLO alerting configured and tested
Security & Compliance: KMS integration tested for customer keys, audit logs capturing request-level metadata enabled; security review completed and signed-off
Load: validated with synthetic workload matching expected GA traffic 2x peak (capacity reserve), autoscaling policies cover bursts without >5% tail-latency degradation
Docs: public docs and quickstarts published; internal runbook for incidents and rollback procedures created
Rollout gating: internal dogfood (1 week) -> alpha with 3 customers (2 weeks) -> gradual beta (3 weeks) -> GA, each gate must meet SLOs and no unresolved P0/P1 bugs
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal dogfood on dedicated env (team members only) for 7 days; smoke tests and SDK examples validated
Phase 1: Alpha with 3 trusted customers; restrict traffic to 10% of GA capacity; collect feedback and perf metrics
Phase 2: Beta opt-in for existing paid customers; enable canaries that start at 1% and ramp to 25% over 7 days if SLOs hold
Phase 3: General Availability with full billing and quotas; announce GA and publish migration guide
Rollback strategy: immediate traffic switch to fallback model variant and downgrade to last stable runtime; pre-prepared rollback runbook in Ops playbook
launch_checklist: Finalize API contract and publish OpenAPI spec
Merge SDK PRs (JS #4532, Python #2281) and cut SDK releases
Publish public docs and quickstarts (confluence -> docs.redwood.ai)
Run full load test (2x expected GA) and confirm capacity/latency targets
Create monitoring dashboards and SLO alerts; test alert escalation paths
Security review completed and KMS test matrix validated
Billing & quotas configured in console and validated with test accounts
Canary and traffic routing policies configured in runtime; fallback model variants defined
Complete PR checklist items: feature flags, telemetry events, tracing hooks
Prepare incident runbook, on-call rotations, and postmortem templates
GA announcement copy and developer migration notes drafted
notes: Model mapping: catalog will include small/medium/large variants with recommended default per route; allow customer pinning to model version
Cost controls: enable per-token cost attribution and optimize default batching/caching suggestions via Redwood Optimize
Compatibility: ensure older SDK versions receive deprecation warnings; provide a compatibility shim for v1 clients
Open questions: final decision on per-request metadata retention window (30d vs 90d) and default embedding vector dimensionality for legacy models
